corneille-oeuvres-marty-laveaux-t5:
Tome five of the 1862 Corneille carries the edition's claim on its title page. The text was reviewed on the oldest printings and on the author's own copies. Unpublished pieces, variants, notices, and notes were added to enrich the set.

Remaining plays share space here with the tools that make the edition lasting. Variant readings, background notes, and records of past staging fill the back matter. Such tools turned a reading text into a scholar's bedrock. All modern study of France's first great dramatist rests on this work. Readers who want Corneille whole, with his changes and his stage history intact, still start with Marty-Laveaux.
kindred-sayings-part5:
Part Five, from 1930, completes Woodward's Book of the Kindred Sayings. The Samyutta Nikaya's final books stand in English at last here. A landmark of Buddhist translation reaches its hard-won finish line.

The last groups of discourses round out themes begun decades earlier. Old age, death, and release frame many of the closing talks. Rhys Davids began the set, and Woodward's hand completes its arc. The Pali Text Society's brave project earns its capstone in this part. Readers gain the whole themed canon in one historic English version at last. The set's close feels like the end of a long pilgrimage.
